title: Ethics in financial reporting
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:32Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank covers honest financial reporting, accounting standards and audits; the closest, corporate social responsibility, is about going beyond legal duties rather than meeting reporting obligations.

draft.title: Ethics in financial reporting
card: Financial reports show how a business is performing. Owners, investors, lenders and the tax office rely on them to make decisions.
reports must give a true and fair view of the business. Profits, debts and assets must not be overstated or hidden.
businesses follow accounting standards, which are agreed rules for how to prepare reports. An audit is a check of the accounts by an independent accountant, who is not an employee of the business.
Misleading reports can break the law and may lead to penalties. They also cost the business the trust of investors, who may then be unwilling to put money in.
draft.remember: Honest reports, set standards and independent audits protect the people who rely on the accounts.

a.q: What is the purpose of an independent audit of a business's accounts?
opts: To check that the reports give a true and fair view
To raise the business's profit for the year
To reduce the amount of tax the business must pay
To set the accounting standards the business follows
a.why: An audit is a check by someone independent that the accounts are honest and follow the standards. It does not change the profit or set the rules. Standards are agreed separately and the auditor checks against them.
a.clue: Think about what an outside checker tests.

b.q: Dana's Tiles in Geelong records sales that have not yet happened, so its profit looks higher before it asks a bank for a loan. Which is the main ethical problem?
opts: The report is misleading, so lenders cannot trust it
The report shows a profit that is too low to impress
The report was not prepared by an employee of the business
The report uses ratios instead of raw dollar figures
b.why: Recording sales that have not happened overstates profit, so the report does not give a true and fair view. The bank may lend on false information, and the owner may face legal penalties. Using ratios is not the problem, as ratios are a normal part of analysis.
b.clue: Who relies on the report, and is it honest?

a.best: To check that the reports give a true and fair view

b.best: The report is misleading, so lenders cannot trust it
